validation_criteria: G1: on the drain, a Claude seat's in-turn output_write gate and the seal judge by the same genome (the run's, from its store): what one accepts the other accepts, and a seal rejection is returned to the chair in-turn first
G2: an output_write whose tool result says ok:false is never captured for sealing, whether is_error is true, false or absent

G3: in checkWritable/write, a top-level property that is not required and is null is removed before validation, hashing and writing; required nulls and nulls inside arrays are untouched; the caller's object is not mutated
G4: both seal briefs tell the chair to omit an optional field it has no value for and never send null
R: the live cde960ea payload shape (change-verdict, decision_ref:null) seals through runGig without the key
G5 (O5): the drain refuses a Claude chair, naming the type, before spawning anything, when a run-registry type does not reload through the loader unchanged
G6: on the server door, the seat's engine child judges by the genome the door was bootstrapped with, from any cwd (including one with its own genome, and one with no build)

testing_method: vitest, example-based. G1 drives the real drainChairInvoker and the real claude invoker spawn. A stand-in claude on PATH (tests/_support/gate_fake_claude.mjs) reads the per-gig --mcp-config, starts the engine server it names over stdio (or http) with the MCP SDK client, and calls output_write, so the in-turn gate the law sees is the real server. The run's genome comes from reconstructGenome over a store row whose change-verdict is v2 and requires org_ticket, which the file genome's closed v1 forbids, so a gate built from the wrong genome shows up in either direction. G2 drives captureOutputWrites over CLI-shaped stream-json. G3 and R drive the output store and runGig on the repo genome. Plants were applied to a scratch copy of src, observed red, and reverted: the file-genome engine child (G1a/G1b), a validation-only strip (G3b, R), stripping required nulls (G3c), a recursive strip (G3d). A sketched fix (materialising the run registry's types as the child's COLTRANE_GENOME) turned G1 green, so the fixture can pass. SUSPECTS. (iii) path skips validate mode: CONFIRMED from source and reproduced (G1a red at origin/main: the mcp-config names servers [] and no engine server). drainChairInvoker (src/cli.ts) builds makeClaudeInvoker({registry, model, timeout_ms}) with no sealVia and no mcpServerConfigs, so a drained Claude seat seals from text. No in-turn gate exists; the seal is the only judgment. The drain's completions seats do use a validate-pinned source over the store registry, so their gates agree. (i) child holds another genome: LATENT. The fix for (iii) would walk into it. The engine child is bootstrapServerDeps(COLTRANE_GENOME ?? cwd), which is the file genome, while the drain seals against the org store's types. Observed with the plant: the file child accepted a payload the store seal refuses (missing org_ticket) and refused one it accepts (additionalProperties org_ticket). (ii) rejection without is_error: Not the live cause. createColtraneServer sets isError: !result.ok. But captureOutputWrites trusts only the CLI's is_error and never reads the ok:false body, so G2 hardens it. ROUND 2 (after the implementer's 769d6de): the shared fixtures are deep-frozen and every law is handed its own structuredClone, so G3e can fail in a full-file run. G2e shows the is_error flag refusing on its own. G5 feeds drainChairInvoker a run registry holding a type the loader drops on reload. G6 bootstraps the server door on a run root holding the org's change-verdict v2, then chdirs into a directory with its own genome (file v1, dist symlinked so the relative entry resolves) and into a bare directory. A scratch fix turned G6 green and was reverted: an absolute entry plus COLTRANE_GENOME set to the bootstrap root in the engine config.
